lc-1.author: Forge
lc-1.explanation: Scan left to right. Before storing a value, look for its complement among earlier values. This prevents using an element twice. Input: a JSON array on the first line and the target on the second.
lc-1.complexity: Expected O(n) time, O(n) extra space.

lc-217.author: Forge
lc-217.explanation: Each item is new exactly when it is absent from the set of earlier items. Stop at the first duplicate. Input: one JSON array.
lc-217.complexity: Expected O(n) time and O(n) space.
lc-217.source:
import json
values = json.loads(input())
seen = set()
duplicate = False
for value in values:
    if value in seen:
        duplicate = True
        break
    seen.add(value)
print(str(duplicate).lower())

lc-704.author: Forge
lc-704.explanation: Maintain an inclusive interval containing every remaining candidate. A comparison eliminates the midpoint and one entire side. Input: sorted JSON array, then the target.
lc-704.complexity: O(log n) time and O(1) space.
lc-704.source:
import json
values = json.loads(input())
target = int(input())
left, right = 0, len(values) - 1
answer = -1
while left <= right:
    mid = left + (right - left) // 2
    if values[mid] == target:
        answer = mid
        break
    if values[mid] < target:
        left = mid + 1
    else:
        right = mid - 1
print(answer)

lc-20.explanation: The stack contains unmatched opening brackets. Every closing bracket must match the latest opening one. The stack must be empty at the end. Input: one line of brackets.

lc-70.author: Forge
lc-70.explanation: The last move is one step or two steps. Their disjoint possibilities give ways(n)=ways(n-1)+ways(n-2). Keep only the last two counts. Input: positive n.
lc-70.source:
n = int(input())
previous, current = 1, 1
for step in range(2, n + 1):
    previous, current = current, previous + current
print(current)

cf-4-A.explanation: Two positive even parts have an even total of at least four. Conversely, for any such total, choosing two as the first part leaves a positive even second part.

cf-71-A.complexity: O(total input length) time, O(longest word) storage.

cf-231-A.author: Forge
cf-231-A.explanation: Count a task only when at least two of the three opinions are positive. Each row is independent.
cf-231-A.source:
n = int(input())
solved = 0
for _ in range(n):
    opinions = list(map(int, input().split()))
    if sum(opinions) >= 2:
        solved += 1
print(solved)

cf-282-A.author: Forge
cf-282-A.explanation: The position of X does not affect the increment or decrement. Inspect the sign and update the running value.
cf-282-A.source:
n = int(input())
value = 0
for _ in range(n):
    operation = input().strip()
    value += 1 if '+' in operation else -1

at-abc086_a.author: Forge
at-abc086_a.explanation: A product is odd precisely when both factors are odd. Check the parity without multiplying large values.
at-abc086_a.source:

at-abc081_a.author: Forge
at-abc081_a.explanation: Count the ones in the three-character input. A zero contributes nothing.
at-abc081_a.complexity: O(length of input) time, O(1) extra space.

at-abc081_b.author: Forge
at-abc081_b.explanation: One operation is possible only while every number is even. Divide the whole array once and repeat. Positive inputs guarantee termination.
at-abc081_b.complexity: O(n log(max a)) time, O(n) space.
at-abc081_b.source:
n = int(input())
values = list(map(int, input().split()))
operations = 0
while all(value % 2 == 0 for value in values):
    values = [value // 2 for value in values]
    operations += 1
print(operations)

at-abc083_b.author: Forge
at-abc083_b.explanation: Enumerate each candidate, compute its digit sum, and add the candidate if the sum lies in the inclusive requested interval.
at-abc083_b.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(log n) temporary space.
at-abc083_b.source:
n, low, high = map(int, input().split())
answer = 0
for value in range(1, n + 1):
    digit_sum = sum(int(digit) for digit in str(value))
    if low <= digit_sum <= high:
        answer += value
print(answer)

at-abc088_b.author: Forge
at-abc088_b.explanation: Sort descending. Optimal play takes the largest remaining card, so alternating positions belong to alternating players.
at-abc088_b.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
at-abc088_b.source:
n = int(input())
cards = sorted(map(int, input().split()), reverse=True)
difference = 0
for turn, value in enumerate(cards):
    difference += value if turn % 2 == 0 else -value
print(difference)

at-dp_a.author: Forge
at-dp_a.explanation: Let cost[i] be the least cost to reach stone i. Its last jump is from i-1 or i-2, so compare those two valid predecessors.
at-dp_a.source:
n = int(input())
height = list(map(int, input().split()))
cost = [0] * n
for i in range(1, n):
    cost[i] = cost[i - 1] + abs(height[i] - height[i - 1])
    if i >= 2:
        alternative = cost[i - 2] + abs(height[i] - height[i - 2])
        cost[i] = min(cost[i], alternative)
print(cost[-1])

at-dp_b.author: Forge
at-dp_b.explanation: Use the same least-cost state as Frog 1 but consider every predecessor at most k positions away. Never read a negative index as a valid predecessor.
at-dp_b.source:
n, k = map(int, input().split())
height = list(map(int, input().split()))
cost = [float('inf')] * n
cost[0] = 0
for i in range(1, n):
    for jump in range(1, min(k, i) + 1):
        candidate = cost[i-jump] + abs(height[i] - height[i-jump])
        cost[i] = min(cost[i], candidate)
print(cost[-1])

at-dp_c.author: Forge
at-dp_c.explanation: Store the best total ending in each activity today. For each choice, use the best total from a different activity yesterday; write into a fresh array to avoid mixing days.
at-dp_c.source:
n = int(input())
best = [0, 0, 0]
for day in range(n):
    points = list(map(int, input().split()))
    next_best = [0, 0, 0]
    for activity in range(3):
        next_best[activity] = points[activity] + max(best[j] for j in range(3) if j != activity)
    best = next_best
print(max(best))
